newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dollar seen capped by German rate uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen capped by German rate uncertainty.

text.p: The dollar remained on firm ground against the mark on Thursday, but fresh gains were expected to be blocked by growing expectations of a German interest rate hike, Singapore dealers said.
"Lately most of the momentum has been generated from the mark and now there might be a change in the mark's value because of the monetary policy implications," a U.S. bank dealer said.

The Bundesbank hinted it may start to tighten the reins of monetary policy, a move seen as necessary to stem the mark's decline, when it refused to specify last week where the rate for its key securities repurchase tender would be in late August.
The dealer said a rise in sterling/mark had driven morning activity but he added that the cross was unlikely to be pushed up much further once Europe opened.
"I expect there'll be some more short-covering and then we'll be in a consolidation phase," he said.
He said the dollar looked well supported at 1.8350 marks but it should be capped around 1.8410/20 marks for the rest of the Asian session.
Dealers said the dollar looked firm above the 118 yen level but lacked momentum to climb much higher than 118.50 yen.
The dollar was earlier dragged down to a low of 117.78 yen on stop-loss sales led by U.S. operators, but Japanese investors' purchases kept it well supported near that level.
